description: Search the VERBATIM authority corpus behind Jobsite's training: 29 CFR regulation text (per-section, with citations), the CA/WA/OR state rules for heat illness and wildfire smoke, plus OSHA interpretations and NIOSH/CDC/EPA technical guidance the training cites. Use this when the user asks what an authority ACTUALLY SAYS — exact rule language, a specific citation ('what does 1926.501 require'), trigger heights, employer duties — and quote the returned text with its citation heading and jurisdiction. EVERY match carries an `authority` field: T1 is binding law, T2 is an agency interpretation and T3 is technical guidance. READ IT BEFORE YOU CHARACTERISE THE MATCH — quote a T2/T3 match as what that agency recommends or says, NEVER as what a regulation requires, and never call it a rule. This is DISTINCT from search_training_source (what Jobsite's TRAINING teaches, paraphrased) — prefer search_law_corpus when the user wants the source itself. The corpus spans the topics Jobsite trains on plus the authorities they cite, NOT all of 29 CFR: an empty result means 'not in the corpus', never 'no such rule exists'.

jurisdiction.description: Optional filter. Omit to search all jurisdictions (federal is most of the corpus).

limit.description: Max sections to return. Defaults to 4, cap 8.

query.description: Plain-words regulatory question or a citation number — 'fall protection trigger height', '1926.501', 'silica exposure control plan'.

name: search_law_corpus
